parole.significato: A factory of the East India Company for the purchase, on advances, of native piece goods etc.
parole.testo: From Hindi [Term?], from Portuguese [Term?] (“a place where goods are manufactured; a depot for such goods”).

parole.significato: A South Asian female servant, maid or nanny, historically, often one working for Europeans in South Asia.
parole.testo: From various Indian languages (e.g. Hindi आया (āyā, “dry nurse, nanny”)), from Portuguese aia (“nurse, governess”), from Latin avia (“grandmother”).
Borrowed from Hindi गोभी (gobhī), from Portuguese couve (“cabbage”), from Latin caulis. Doublet of caulis, cole, and kale.
Borrowed from Hindi मिस्त्री (mistrī), from Portuguese mestre.
